title: Skeleton + bli frontier on GitHub

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

body:
## Parent

#1

## What to build

In a repo whose `bli.toml` names GitHub as the issue tracker, `bli frontier [--parent <id>]` lists the **frontier**: the open child tickets of a parent that have no open blockers and no assignee. It prints a readable list, or the ticket ID, title and URL for each ticket with `--json`. Without `--parent` it uses the configured default parent, and fails with a hint when there is none. Without a `bli.toml` it fails with a hint about creating one.

This is the first slice, so it also lays down what every later ticket builds on: the Rust crate, a `flake.nix` that builds `bli`, config loading, a command layer that depends only on the issue tracker interface, the GitHub adapter calling `gh` through a single process-runner interface, the `--json` and stderr/exit-code conventions, and the test harness for both seams in the spec (fakes for the command layer; command-line translation and saved-JSON parsing for adapters).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `nix build` produces a `bli` binary; `cargo install --path .` also works
- [ ] `bli frontier --parent <n>` lists open sub-issues with no open blockers and no assignee, and leaves out closed, blocked and assigned ones
- [ ] `bli frontier` uses `[tracker] parent` when it is set, and fails with a hint when neither it nor `--parent` is given
- [ ] Running any command without `bli.toml` fails with a hint and a non-zero exit
- [ ] `--json` output has a stable shape (ID, title, URL per ticket); errors go to stderr with a non-zero exit
- [ ] `bli` never prompts interactively
- [ ] Command-layer tests run against a fake issue tracker; GitHub adapter tests check the `gh` command line and parse saved real `gh` output

title: Fan-out on herdr: lane start, lane list, fan-out skill

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

body:
## Parent

#1

## What to build

From inside herdr, `/fan-out` in a GitHub-tracked repo starts real **lanes**. The thin fan-out skill (in this repo) calls `bli frontier`, shows the developer the tickets and asks before starting, then calls `bli lane start <ticket>...`. For each ticket, `lane start` fetches, checks that the **base** exists on the remote, asks the lane host to create a lane from the remote base on a branch named from the configured pattern (default `ticket/{id}-{slug}`, slug from the ticket title, `--slug` to override), records the lane's base with its branch, starts Claude in bypass-permissions mode with the configured prompt (default `/implement {ticket_url}`), and **claims** the ticket. `bli lane list` shows every lane with its ticket, branch, base, and the host's status hint, found by matching the host's live list against the branch pattern (ADR 0001).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The lane host interface exists, with a herdr adapter: detect inside-host, create a lane, start the agent with a prompt, list lanes with a status hint
- [ ] `lane start` fails clearly when not inside the configured lane host, and when the base isn't on the remote
- [ ] Lanes branch from the remote copy of the base after a fetch, never the local branch
- [ ] Branch names follow the configured pattern; the slug is lowercase kebab-case from the first five words of the title; `--slug` overrides it
- [ ] Each lane's base is recorded as git branch config and read back by `lane list`
- [ ] The ticket is assigned to the current user after its lane exists
- [ ] Tickets that already have a lane or a claim are skipped and reported as skipped; `frontier` leaves out tickets that already have a lane
- [ ] Lanes start one at a time, and each lane's outcome is reported separately in the JSON output
- [ ] `lane list` finds lanes only by branch pattern, with no stored state, and reports the host's status as a hint
- [ ] The fan-out skill confirms the ticket list with the developer before calling `lane start`, and reports a table afterwards
- [ ] Command-layer tests use a fake lane host and real git in a temporary repo with a local bare remote; herdr adapter tests check command lines and parse saved herdr JSON

title: Remove-lane: lane inspect, lane rm, remove-lane skill

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

body:
## Parent

#1

## What to build

`/remove-lane <lane>` tears down one lane safely. The thin remove-lane skill calls `bli lane inspect <lane>`, shows the developer exactly what removal would lose, gets an explicit yes (with separate explicit choices for `--force` and branch deletion), then calls `bli lane rm`. A lane can be named by ticket ID, branch, checkout path or host workspace ID.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Naming a lane that matches nothing, or more than one, fails with the candidates listed
- [ ] `lane inspect` reports uncommitted and untracked files, commits on no remote, the upstream, PR state, and the host's status hint
- [ ] `lane rm` removes the lane's workspace and checkout through the lane host; the local branch is deleted only with `--delete-branch`
- [ ] `lane rm` refuses dirty or untracked files without `--force`, and refuses `--delete-branch` with commits on no remote without `--force`
- [ ] `lane rm` always refuses the main checkout, and the lane the caller is running from
- [ ] Deleting the branch also removes the lane's recorded base
- [ ] The remove-lane skill never calls `lane rm` without an explicit yes, and supports a dry run (inspect only)
- [ ] Every refusal rule is covered by command-layer tests against real git

title: Fan-in ships finished lanes: lane read, lane ship, fan-in skill

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

body:
## Parent

#1

## What to build

`/fan-in` moves finished lanes forward. The thin fan-in skill calls `bli lane list`, and for each lane that isn't clearly working, calls `bli lane read <ticket>` to get the agent's recent output and judges it: still going (leave it), asking a question (show the developer), stalled (report it), or finished. For a finished lane it writes the PR body with the `pr` skill and calls `bli lane ship <ticket> --body-file <file>`, which pushes the branch and opens a PR against the lane's recorded base. On GitHub Issues the PR closes the ticket on merge.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The code host interface exists (GitHub via `gh`): push a branch, find a head branch's PR in any state, open a PR against a base with a body file
- [ ] `lane read` returns the lane agent's recent output through the lane host
- [ ] `lane ship` opens the PR against the recorded base, not the default base
- [ ] `lane ship` refuses when the lane has no commits beyond its base
- [ ] Rerunning `lane ship` reports the existing PR instead of opening a second one
- [ ] On GitHub Issues the PR body closes the ticket on merge
- [ ] `lane list` shows each lane's PR state
- [ ] `bli` never merges a PR
- [ ] The fan-in skill bases its decision on the lane's output; the status hint is advisory only

title: Fan-in cleans up merged lanes: lane clean, on-merge action

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

body:
## Parent

#1

## What to build

After the developer merges a lane's PR, `/fan-in` cleans the lane up by calling `bli lane clean`. It removes every lane whose PR was merged (workspace, checkout, local branch and recorded base), applies the configured `on_merge` action to each ticket (`close` by default, `none`, or `{ status = "..." }`), and fast-forwards the main checkout when it is on the cleaned lane's base. Lanes whose PR was closed without merging are reported and left alone. The fan-in skill then reports which tickets merging the open PRs would unblock.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A lane counts as merged when its PR is merged, including squash merges whose remote branch was deleted
- [ ] `lane clean` removes merged lanes through the same removal path as `lane rm`
- [ ] The `on_merge` action is applied per cleaned ticket; on GitHub, `close` is a no-op when the PR already closed the ticket
- [ ] The main checkout is fast-forwarded when it is on the lane's base, even with uncommitted changes, and left alone otherwise
- [ ] Closed-not-merged lanes are reported, not removed
- [ ] The fan-in skill reports the tickets that merging the open PRs would unblock
- [ ] Command-layer tests cover a squash-merged lane, each `on_merge` value, and fast-forwarding with uncommitted changes

title: bli doctor

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

body:
## Parent

#1

## What to build

`bli doctor` checks a repo's setup before a fan-out, and warns on each check that fails: `git`, `gh` and the configured lane host's CLI are installed; the issue tracker's credentials work; and the lane host launches Claude in bypass-permissions mode (on herdr, `bli` passes the flag itself, so the check passes when herdr is installed and reachable).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bli doctor` reports each check as pass or warn, as text or `--json`
- [ ] It exits non-zero when any check fails
- [ ] Each adapter contributes its own checks, so later lane hosts and trackers add theirs without changing the command
- [ ] Missing tools, a failed credential check and the permission-mode check are each covered by tests against fakes

title: ClickUp as issue tracker

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

body:
## Parent

#1

## What to build

With `kind = "clickup"` in `bli.toml`, the whole lane loop runs against ClickUp. A native HTTP adapter (API v2) supplies the frontier from the parent task's subtasks, with "waiting on" dependencies as blockers and the assignee as claim, and applies `on_merge` (close or set status). Workspace, list and space IDs come from `[tracker.clickup]`; the API token comes from `CLICKUP_API_TOKEN` in the environment, else the checkout's `.env`, else the main checkout's `.env`. ClickUp Docs and uploads are out of scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `frontier`, `lane start` (claim), and `lane clean` (`on_merge`) work against ClickUp
- [ ] Ticket IDs and URLs use ClickUp's native task IDs, and branch names follow the configured pattern with them
- [ ] The token is found through the env → checkout `.env` → main-checkout `.env` chain, and never read from `bli.toml`
- [ ] The API base is configurable, and adapter tests run against a local stub HTTP server
- [ ] `on_merge = "close"` closes the ticket, because PRs can't close ClickUp tickets
- [ ] `bli doctor` checks the ClickUp token

title: Superset as lane host

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

body:
## Parent

#1

## What to build

With `host = "superset"` in `bli.toml`, the whole lane loop runs in Superset: start, list, read, ship, inspect, remove and clean. The Superset adapter creates lanes with the exact branch name and no Superset branch prefix, detects that it's running inside Superset, maps Superset's agent states onto the status hint, and removes lanes. Claude's bypass-permissions mode lives in Superset's agent preset, so `bli doctor` checks the preset and warns when it's missing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Superset adapter implements every lane host operation
- [ ] Lane branches match the configured pattern exactly, with no Superset prefix
- [ ] Running outside Superset with `host = "superset"` fails clearly
- [ ] Superset's agent states map onto the status hint
- [ ] Removing a lane leaves no Superset workspace and no checkout behind
- [ ] `bli doctor` warns when Superset's Claude preset doesn't launch in bypass-permissions mode
- [ ] Adapter tests check command lines and parse saved Superset JSON

title: Adopt bli in pos-poc

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

body:
## Parent

#1

## What to build

pos-poc switches from its own `fan-out`, `fan-in` and `remove-lane` skills to `bli`. It gets a `bli.toml` (herdr, GitHub, default parent set to its MVP spec issue), the skills installed from this repo the same way as the other skills, and its old copies removed. Then one live run through on herdr + GitHub with a throwaway scratch lane confirms that start, list, read, inspect and rm work against the real tools.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] pos-poc has a committed `bli.toml`, and `bli doctor` passes there
- [ ] pos-poc's skills come from this repo, and the old copies are removed
- [ ] A scratch lane is started, listed, read, inspected and removed live on herdr, and the results are recorded on this ticket
- [ ] No regression against the old skills' safety gates
